text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures remain steady in firmer ground during Bundesbank ews conference, with June future back below 101.01 resistance but seen healthy. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.00, up 0/36 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended the day in fine fettle, recouping morning gains late in the afternoon session after a weak U.S. Philly Fed survey report. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-05/32, up 15/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and interest rate futures underperformed their German counterparts as concerns about France's ability to hit public deficit targets in 1997 and talk of an early election unsettled nervous traders. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.90, down 0.12 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures ended the session in negative territory, with some traders attributing the downturn to comments on EMU by Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer while others said it was just a technical correction after the June contract peaked at 129.05 in the morning. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.38, down 0.14 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were higher after a weak Philly Fed report, prices paid and received rose despite weaker headline number, with the Market gives back some gains as prices components digested, traders see Fed tracking Philly report for signs of demand *Upside seen limited for market as employment data awaited. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-02/32, up 19/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.05 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower as sentiment was weakened by overnight comments by a senior Finance Ministry official, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, said that although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan, there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.77, up 0.18 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw a string of key deals from the major borrowers, including the first sterling bond with a euro redenomination clause, the latter was a 500 million stering deal from the European Investment Bank. The December 2007 issue was priced to yield 12 basis points over an identically dated gilt by lead manager BZW.
